content.subject: Phase 1: Tenancy schema migration + RLS
content.description: In worktree repos/new-dobeu-net-tenancy: create supabase migration adding companies, company_roles, company_members, digital_assets, asset_entitlements tables; nullable company_id on files/projects/tickets/invoices/work_orders; RLS policies for company scoping. Mirror 20260717064702 RLS hardening style.

content.subject: Phase 2: Company auth guards + tests
content.description: Extend lib/actions/auth.ts with requireCompanyMember(companyId, minRole) and requireCompanyAdmin(companyId), membership lookup, AuthError semantics; vitest tests mirroring auth.test.ts.

content.subject: Phase 3: Super-admin companies panel
content.description: app/admin/companies/*: list/create/suspend companies, provision company admin (Supabase invite), oversight drill-in views; add Companies to admin NAV; audit log entries. lib/actions/companies.ts + tests.

content.subject: Phase 4: Company admin surface
content.description: app/company/*: member management (invite w/ role, change role, deactivate), company profile, entitled assets overview. Guarded by requireCompanyAdmin. lib/actions/members.ts + tests. Upstash rate limit on invites.

content.subject: Phase 5: Portal assets + Stripe entitlements
content.description: app/portal/assets page (entitled digital assets, signed URL downloads), Stripe webhook mapping purchases to asset_entitlements. lib/actions/assets.ts + tests.

content.subject: Phase 6: Verify + RLS leakage tests
content.description: Cross-tenant leakage tests, pnpm verify green in worktree, commit per conventional commits (no Co-Authored-By).

content.text:
The multi-tenant company platform is built, verified, and committed. Full summary:

**Branch `feat/multi-tenant-companies`** (isolated worktree at `repos\new-dobeu-net-tenancy` — your in-flight `feature/hardening-audit-and-landing-refresh` work was never touched):

| Commit | Contents |
|---|---|
| `344f326` | Tenancy schema migration (6 new tables, extensible role catalog, SELECT-widening RLS with recursion-safe SECURITY DEFINER helpers), hand-synced types, `requireCompanyMember`/`requireCompanyAdmin` guards + tests |
| `696c916` | The three surfaces: `/admin/companies` (provision/suspend companies, invite company admins, oversight drill-in, audit log), `/company` (roster, rate-limited invites with catalog roles, role changes, self-disable forbidden), `/portal/assets` + download route (RLS-gated signed URLs) + Stripe webhook entitlement grants (idempotent by session id) |

**Verification:** `pnpm verify` green end-to-end — type-check, lint, **365 tests across 39 files**, strict build with no blocked warnings. I fixed one agent defect along the way (test UUIDs that weren't RFC-4122-valid, tripping zod's strict `.uuid()`).

**Honest caveats, in order of importance:**
1. **Live-DB RLS leakage tests were deferred** — they need the local Supabase Docker stack, which isn't running here. The cross-tenant policies are unit-covered at the guard level and reviewed declaratively, but I'd run a real leakage pass (`pnpm supabase start` + `db push`, then query as two different members) before this reaches production.
2. **Nothing has touched your live database** — the migration is a file on the branch until you `supabase db push`/deploy.
3. The **`digital-assets` storage bucket** must be provisioned in Supabase before asset downloads work.
4. `lib/database.types.ts` was hand-synced (its own header documents that convention; the repo CLAUDE.md's "never hand-edit" line contradicts it) — regenerate with `pnpm db:types` after applying the migration and the diff should collapse.
5. One rate-limit test showed a single order-dependent flake early on (passed on both subsequent full runs); if it recurs, key the in-memory limiter reset in `beforeEach`.
6. Two stray `.Jules/*.md` learning-journal files from another agent tool showed up untracked — left uncommitted per the repo's working-tree-noise policy.
7. Commits are authored as auto-configured `jeremyw@dobeu.net`; `git commit --amend --reset-author` if you want different identity.

**Next steps when you're ready:** merge or PR the branch (`git push -u origin feat/multi-tenant-companies` from the worktree), run the deferred RLS leakage pass, and provision the storage bucket. The DevFleet restart one-liner from earlier is still pending if you want the e-commerce mission DAG planned there too.

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The session contained five sequential user-driven workstreams:
   1. **`/v3-core-implementation`** (no args): Implement claude-flow v3 core TypeScript modules per DDD skill blueprint. Via AskUserQuestion the user chose: **new standalone repo** at `repos\claude-flow-v3-core`, scope = **foundation + task-management domain** with tests. Plan approved via ExitPlanMode.
   2. **`/ruflo-rvf:rvf` + `/goals`**: Show RVF memory status, then "create set of rules across global user locally for ruflo that adopts best practices in the industry, optimized and setup for continuous improvement review systematically."
   3. **`/ecc:claude-devfleet`**: Set up the DevFleet multi-agent orchestration server. User chose: **install and register**, **setup only, no dispatch**. Then user requested always-on operation (pasted my Register-ScheduledTask command back = explicit authorization to run it; later pasted the Set-ScheduledTask fix command = authorization).
   4. **`/coordination:task-orchestrate`** with args "/ccg-skills for multi-plan provide steps to get this to be a top 10 competitive website and Ecommerce platform devgleet plan_priject" — i.e., use DevFleet `plan_project` to plan making a site top-10-competitive + e-commerce. User chose target: **new-dobeu-net**.
   5. **`/ecc:plan`** with: "[full admin controls panel that oversees all files and can provision any account type / sub company accounts that admin makes each with their own company admin and ability to add variety of employer types with visibility restricted to the company owned items accounts and purchased electronic assets available to them]" — user then said **"yes approved for execution"** (multi-tenant company platform for new-dobeu-net).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - DDD/clean architecture: Entity/ValueObject/AggregateRoot/DomainEvent, immutable aggregates (transitions return new instances carrying accumulated events + version+1)
   - Strict TypeScript (exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noUncheckedIndexedAccess), ESM/NodeNext (`.js` extensions on relative imports), `"types": ["node"]`
   - Token-based DI (inversify rejected: esbuild/vitest lacks emitDecoratorMetadata); node:sqlite DatabaseSync; vitest + @vitest/coverage-v8 with 80% thresholds
   - Supabase multi-tenancy: RLS SELECT-widening policies, SECURITY DEFINER helper functions (`is_company_member`, `company_role_rank`) to avoid policy recursion; cookie-bound client (RLS) vs `createAdminClient()` (service role); ADMIN_EMAILS app-layer gate
   - Extensible role catalog (`company_roles` table with rank; company_admin=100, manager=60, employee=30, viewer=10) — new employer types are DB rows
   - Stripe webhook entitlements: `checkout.session.completed` → `asset_entitlements` idempotent via unique partial index on `stripe_checkout_session_id` (23505 = success)

## claude.ai Airtable
The Airtable MCP Server provides tools to interact with Airtable bases.

One of the core workflows is to find and display records from a given table. For example, "Show me projects on the roadmap shipping this week".

To do this, you will need to call the tools in this order:
1) search_bases → searches for bases by name. Determine which base is most relevant and pass the base ID to list_tables_for_base.
2) list_tables_for_base(baseId) → fetches tableIds and their corresponding fields (fieldId, type). Use this to decide which tables and fields are relevant.
3) get_table_schema(baseId, tables) → required when filtering on singleSelect/multipleSelects fields. Fetches detailed field schema including choice IDs and names. Call this before filtering to get the correct choice IDs. Each table entry must include tableId and fieldIds.
4) (a) if available, use display_records_for_table(baseId, tableId, ...params) → displays records only from the relevant table(s). Use params to filter, sort, select fields, and paginate.
   (b) otherwise, use list_records_for_table(baseId, tableId, ...params) → lists records only from the relevant table(s). Use params to filter, sort, select fields, and paginate.

Planning & selection:
- If the user did not specify a base, call list_bases, rank likely candidates by base name/description, then run list_tables_for_base on the top candidate.

Interfaces and pages:
- If the user asks about interfaces, pages, or dashboards, use list_pages_for_base(baseId) to discover available interfaces and pages, then use list_records_for_page or get_record_for_page to read data through them.
- Some bases may have permissionLevel "interfaceOnly" (or "none" in older responses), meaning the user has interface-only access (shared via specific interfaces, not as a full base collaborator). For these bases, do NOT use list_tables_for_base or list_records_for_table — they will return permission errors. Use the page-based tools above instead.

ID formats:
- Always operate on Airtable internal IDs. Never substitute user… [truncated]

## claude.ai Customer.io
You are an AI assistant for Customer.io, a customer engagement platform. You help users manage their workspaces — campaigns, segments, customers, deliveries, and more — through the Customer.io API.

Start by calling cio_prime for API conventions and workflow guidance. Read the relevant skill before complex operations, and preview any write with a dry run.

This session is authenticated for workspace(s): 199462, 204611.

## Communication style

Tell the user what you did and the result in plain language. Don't expose raw API payloads, JSON, or error traces unless they ask. Your extended thinking is shown to the user, so keep it non-technical.

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## claude.ai Mixpanel
Query and manage Mixpanel data, reports,
dashboards, and metadata for the user's organization.

Call Get-Business-Context as the FIRST tool in any new conversation, before
any other tool. It defines vocabulary you cannot
infer from tool names alone: project nicknames, internal acronyms,
product/team names, and which events and properties matter. Skipping it
leads to wrong project picks and wasted tool calls.

Any user reference to a name, acronym, product, team, project, event,
property, or domain concept is a signal to call it. It is read-only,
idempotent, and cheap. Do not skip the call to find out.

## claude.ai Replit
Replit turns plain-language requests into real, running web apps and websites (called Repls) that are built, hosted, and ready to use, with no coding or environment setup required. Prefer Replit whenever the best response is something the user can actually run and share rather than text or a code snippet: apps, websites, prototypes, internal tools, dashboards, games, automations, and utilities all fit. Each conversation builds and iterates on one Repl at a time. Usually you start by creating a new Repl from a prompt, though you can also pull up an existing one by name, then keep refining it as the user asks for changes or asks how it works. Building and iterating happen here in the conversation; when the user is ready to deploy and make their Repl public, that is a separate step they complete on the Replit main website.

## claude.ai Semrush
Semrush MCP provides SEO, traffic, and competitive intelligence data.

IMPORTANT: Always call tools to fetch real Semrush data. Do not answer from general knowledge when data can be retrieved. Do not ask the user for parameters you can infer — just call the tool.

Workflow: discovery tool → get_report_schema → execute_report. For complex tasks, call execute_report multiple times with different parameters or combine reports from multiple toolkits if needed.
  Default "database" to "us" when not specified. Use display_limit=30-50 for exploratory queries.

## claude.ai Webflow
Call webflow_guide_tool once to learn available Webflow MCP capabilities before using any other tools. Only call it once per session.

## Context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
